newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch plan law to curb anti-takeover defences.
newsitem.headline: Dutch plan law to curb anti-takeover defences.

text.p: A new law curbing Dutch companies' defences against hostile takeover bids will be sent to parliament for approval during the new legislative year which was opened on Tuesday, the Finance Ministry said.
The law will enable long-term shareholders with stakes of 70 percent or more to override anti-takeover defences which have previously rendered Dutch companies impregnable to hostile bids.

Under the changes hostile bidders will be able to submit their bids for review to a commercial court which will rule in their favour if the takeover is judged not to threaten the interests of the target company.

"The bill aims...to strengthen the position of shareholders, to enhance the efficiency of the takeover market and to improve the climate for foreign investment in the Netherlands," the ministry said in documents accompanying the 1997 budget.
Steps will also be taken in the new parliamentary year to tighten up current legislation outlawing insider trading.

The ministry said the law will be amended to outlaw all trade in securities based on privileged access to price-sensitive information. At present the law requires the public prosecutor to prove conclusively that insider dealings resulted in a profit or were intended to produce a profit.
The Netherlands made insider trading a criminal offence in 1989, but to date the few cases to have been prosecuted have not led to convictions.
